findings.title: Persistent storage write without TTL management
findings.description: A contract entry point writes to persistent storage but does not call `extend_ttl`, `set_ttl`, or `bump` in the same function or in the intra-file helpers it calls. Persistent entries have a time-to-live; if it is not extended, stored data can expire and be lost. TTL may legitimately be managed elsewhere (for example in a separate maintenance entry point), so this is a low-confidence signal.
findings.evidence: persistent storage write without TTL extension in `set`: env . storage () . persistent () . set (& DataKey :: Value , & value)
findings.remediation: When writing persistent data that must survive, extend its time-to-live with `storage().persistent().extend_ttl(...)` after the write. Prefer a single, well-documented TTL policy for the contract. If TTL is managed centrally, suppress this rule for the function.

findings.title: Authorization after state mutation
findings.description: A contract entry point mutates storage before calling `require_auth`. The authorization check must run before the effect, otherwise a rejected call may already have changed state on some paths and the ordering indicates a logic bug.
findings.evidence: storage mutation before authorization in `set`: env . storage () . persistent () . set (& DataKey :: Value , & value)
findings.remediation: Authorize the caller at the start of the entry point, before any storage read or write that depends on the caller. Call `require_auth` or `require_auth_for_args` first, then perform the state change.
